title: Preserve requested stop exits across selected-runtime import boundaries
goal: Repair the demonstrated stop-boundary exit-code loss in a separately identified private SDK derivative, without weakening the failing lifecycle contract.
acceptance: Retain the decommit-v1 failure: a barrier-controlled child with RequestStop(77) before its next kernel import must exit with 77 and never return from that import
Distinguish a pending cooperative stop from an explicit thread exit; audit import/hook, wait, spin and fiber exception consumers and preserve explicit exit behavior
Use an original minimal BSD-compatible patch with exact base, composition, compiler, source, header and library identities; preserve all baseline packages and rebuild every affected consumer
Provide fail-closed preparation/verification and explicit repaired-SDK selection in thread, memory and CPU diagnostics; do not silently substitute it into owned-title preparation
validation: Repeat isolated and combined declaration/shuffled thread contracts on Windows/Linux native and supported sanitizers, including actual instrumented Linux core
Reject result/deadline mutations and stale or modified derivative receipts, headers and libraries; retain baseline failures rather than relabeling them
Record unsupported sanitizer/translated-code coverage and run affected memory/CPU regressions before later title integration
